newsitem.title: UK: BOMB SCARE DELAYS ENGLAND-POLAND SOCCER.
newsitem.headline: BOMB SCARE DELAYS ENGLAND-POLAND SOCCER.

text.p: An international under-21 soccer match between England and Poland was delayed two hours by a bomb scare on Tuesday night, a day after Irish guerrillas blasted a British army barracks in Northern Ireland.
Bomb disposal experts used a controlled explosion to destroy what police described as a suspicious package found at the ground in the central English city of Wolverhampton.
Police said the parcel, found by a steward in a rubbish bin under the main stand, was later found to be harmless.
"At every major sporting event safety checks are carried out and if you find something you would be foolish not to check out the matter," Chief Superintendent Roger Allen said.
"If you ignore the package, let people into the ground and then 40 people are killed...the fear of that basically makes the decision for you."
The match, which was due to start at 1900 GMT, kicked off more than two hours late after the 6,000 crowd was allowed back into the stadium.
